ai.description: *Bufoides kempi* is a small toad reaching 30–35 mm. It is dark brown with a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe and granular skin. Key features include a flattened body and rounded, unwebbed toe tips.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Bufoides kempi* is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow or orange glandular patches on its flanks and limbs, which contrast sharply against its dark skin.
ai.habitat: *Bufoides kempi* inhabits high-altitude, humid subtropical broadleaf forests in the Meghalaya plateau, typically found near rocky streams at elevations of 1,000–1,500m.
ai.behavior: Kemp's Asian Tree Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter and rocky crevices of its humid forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Bufoides kempi* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in water-filled tree holes or rock crevices. It exhibits direct or semi-aquatic development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Bufoides kempi* is endemic to the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests at elevations between 1,000 and 1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Bufoides kempi* consists of a series of high-pitched, pulsed chirps, typically emitted by males perched on wet rock faces near mountain streams.
